watch.name: unanswered-important-email
watch.nl_query: Tell me when someone sends me an email that looks genuinely important and I still haven't replied three days later.

nodes.comment: The two-stage shape a semantic watch is built on. The filter is free and cuts the corpus to inbound mail; recall is cheap and nominates what is topically plausible; the judge is the only expensive stage and sees one document at a time. Raising the threshold spends less and misses more — the shadow period is how you find out which way to move it. There is no direction field on a document: inbound is expressed as a sender who is not you.

semantic.query: important email that needs a reply from me

judge.proposition: This email is genuinely important AND is waiting on a reply from the recipient

nodes.comment: No recall and no judge: this arm exists to cancel, and whether a reply is important is beside the point. A cancel arm that had to be judged would cost a model call for every message you send.

Keyed on the thread, so an arm and the cancel that answers it can only meet if they are about the same conversation. `reset` means a second important message in the same thread restarts the three days rather than being ignored — the question is whether the thread is waiting on you, not whether one message was.
